bugfix._reasoning_help: medium, not xhigh. At xhigh on a ~70k-token evidence payload this pass spent its ENTIRE output cap on thinking - measured at exactly 12288 tokens, the cap - and was cut off before it finished writing the document. Section 2 sits near the top, so the harness reported 'section 2 declared no COMMAND' and burned every retry on the same wall. The reserve now scales with the level, which makes xhigh survivable, but medium is what this pass actually needs: it is tracing a payload through four files, not solving a research problem.

_server_help: INERT UNDER THE vllm PROVIDER - the orchestrator spawns no server, so nothing here is read; vLLM's equivalents are set in qwen-serving/.env (SPEC, CTX, MAX_LEN, EXTRA_ARGS). Kept for switching back to llamacpp. Tuning for the shared llama-server the orchestrator spawns. A property of the SERVER process, not of any one phase, so unlike `sampling` these cannot be sent per request - the server has to be restarted to change them. Read fresh at launch; a malformed block degrades to the values below rather than stopping a model loading. `speculative.type` accepts any value llama.cpp's --spec-type does; "none" is the clean off switch and suppresses the four draft_* knobs rather than passing them to a disabled drafter.

server._batch_help: -b is the logical batch cap and is close to VRAM-free; -ub is the physical one and is what sizes the compute buffer. These were hardcoded to 1024/1024, which put -b BELOW llama.cpp's own 2048 default for no saving. Do not reach for -ub 512 as a way to fit MTP: measured, it takes the draft compute buffer from 1120 to 880 MiB, not to half, because a large part of that allocation is fixed. It was not enough at 163840 and it will not be.
server._speculative_help: Multi-token prediction, MEASURED on this box at 50.44 vs 39.07 tok/s - 1.29x, not the 1.5x the vendor figures imply. It loads no second model (the draft head ships in this GGUF: qwen35 nextn_predict_layers 1) but the draft context allocates its OWN compute buffer, ~1120 MiB at ubatch 1024, and inherits the target's window - this build has no --ctx-size-draft to cap it. That is what decides whether it fits, and it does NOT fit at LLAMACPP_SERVER_CTX 163840. Measured peak VRAM of 24576 MiB: 163840+none 22759 (fits), 163840+mtp OOM, 131072+mtp 23495 (1081 spare), 98304+mtp 21987 (2589 spare). So turning this on means lowering LLAMACPP_SERVER_CTX, and that constant is 163840 for a documented reason - Cline compacts against a hardcoded 128000, so a 131072 server puts a maximal prompt back within ~3k tokens of the wall. Default off: 29% generation is not obviously worth re-opening that failure. Set type to draft-mtp AND lower LLAMACPP_SERVER_CTX together, or not at all.

_sampling_help: Per-phase sampling. `_modes` holds the model card's two presets - thinking wants a wide, unpenalised distribution because the reasoning channel needs room to explore; instruct wants a narrower one with a presence penalty so a non-thinking pass does not restate itself. Each phase names the mode it runs in and may override individual parameters on top of it (temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, presence_penalty, repetition_penalty). Naming the mode rather than restating six numbers is the point: retuning a preset moves every phase that uses it, and an override reads as a deliberate deviation. An unknown parameter name is a startup error, not a silently ignored key. `cline_startup` is the Cline build agent's own turns; distill.py does not run that phase, so its values are applied by the orchestrator as llama-server defaults when it starts the shared server.

_modes._thinking_temperature_help: 0.95 rather than the card's 1.0: a deliberate local tune, carried over from the SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE constant this block replaced. It sits just under the preset rather than far below it - the repetition-loop risk this family shows is at temperatures well under the card's figures, which 0.6 and 0.3 both were.

sampling._engineer_help: The only instruct phase. It transcribes an architecture that has already been decided into a file-by-file build map, and thinking-mode sampling on that job produces invention where transcription was wanted.
sampling._bugfix_sampling_help: A discrete phase, outside the four software-factory passes: it replaces the architect in slot 1 for `!bugfix` runs and is never one stage of the same pipeline.

_prompts_help: Prompt bodies live in Markdown files. Values are paths resolved relative to this config file; an inline string is still accepted for backwards compatibility.

limits._review_help: review_enabled is the master switch: false drops the phase and the loop runs build -> verify -> safety exactly as it did before. Override for a single run with `-e REVIEW_ENABLED=false` without editing this file. The Review phase runs between Build and Verify, scoped to only the files the build phase wrote, so it needs less wall-clock than the phases that sweep the whole project. It is skipped automatically on an iteration where the build wrote nothing. review_thinking_level is the Cline CLI's --thinking flag (reasoning effort): none|low|medium|high|xhigh. Raise it to trade wall-clock for depth of review; an empty string omits the flag and leaves the provider default.
limits._replan_help: Between build iterations, re-run the design passes against .build_issues.md when it has grown this many bytes since the plan was written. Set max_replans to 0 to disable. replan_passes defaults to architect+engineer; narrow it to ["architect"] to halve the GPU cost at the price of a roadmap that no longer matches the revised architecture.
limits._bugfix_help: `!bugfix` swaps the architect for the bugfix pass, which must declare a COMMAND that actually fails before its diagnosis is accepted. bugfix_max_repro_attempts is how many times the pass may be re-run with the observed output fed back; 1 means run the repro once and never retry, 0 disables verification entirely and the diagnosis becomes self-reported. Each attempt after the first costs a design pass plus at most one round of blocker evidence, so 3 is roughly 15-25 minutes of GPU and the review gate will usually return 'still running' before it finishes - that is expected, and `!review` picks it up. bugfix_repro_timeout_secs caps a single run of the declared command.
